newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Gold closes slightly easier at day's low in HK.
newsitem.headline: Gold closes slightly easier at day's low in HK.

text.p: Hong Kong gold closed slightly easier at its day's low on Wednesday following late selling pressure after a day of quiet two-way trading, dealers said.

Morning short-covering from Asian investors pushed gold to a day's high of US$343.50/344.00, but selling interest in late trading pared the gains. Bullion ended at US$342.70/343.20 an ounce against New York's US$343.00/50 close on Tuesday.
"The local market has very quiet, with small amount of short-covering and selling interest," a senior gold dealer said.
"We will just keep watching the other precious metals moves," another dealer said. "Gold is seen remaining trapped in a US$340 to $348 band for this week."
Local gold ended HK$7 lower at HK$3,174 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to -4.00 from its previous fix at -1.00.
